title: status-resolution-exposes-presentation-activity

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat a status or revocation check as privacy-neutral when the act, target, timing, or requesting context of resolution allows an issuer, status provider, or observer to infer credential presentation activity or relationships.

preconditions: A relying party resolves credential, authorization, revocation, or lifecycle status through an observable service or interaction.
The privacy objective requires limiting issuer or status-provider knowledge of where or when a credential is used.
The status result itself may be minimal and semantically correct.

trigger.statement: The status-resolution event exposes a credential-specific or context-specific observation that permits usage correlation, while the verification flow still treats privacy assurance as satisfied.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence describing which parties can observe status-resolution requests and what relationship information those observations reveal.
Evidence of request timing and whether timing can be associated with a presentation or relying-party event.
Cross-context observations sufficient to test whether status-resolution activity creates a join between otherwise separate interactions.
Evidence identifying the status source and any intermediaries able to observe the request.

falsification.condition: The system reports PASS for the privacy proposition even though the status provider can associate credential-specific requests with distinct presentation events.
Assessment examines only the content of the status response and ignores privacy-significant metadata created by making the lookup.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the privacy/correlation tranche.
Research provenance: W3C VC Data Model Threat Model v2.1, Correlation via Status and Revocation Lookup; draft/work in progress, not corpus authority.
